question: At byte-identical inputs, do the MPS and native Metal SSB paths stay inside a strict float32/complex64 bound of an independent double-precision evaluation, and does the frozen fit trajectory survive enabling the batched pair draw?

inputs.note: 512x512 x 192x192 uint16 real acquisition; the export proves every selected value against an independent h5py read (0 mismatches in 2,342,780,928 values)
the executable QuantEM/Python reference; defaults to optuna_batch_size = 2

parameters.brightfield_policy: documented full disk minus one hardware dead pixel (78, 74): 8937 logical, 2464 aperture-active
parameters.precision: exact uint16 raw counts, float32 real, complex64 complex, no binning, no crop, no fast-math path, no CPU fallback in any measured path
parameters.gate_rule: min(absolute float32 bound, 2x the measured single-precision floor of the identical formula evaluated with SciPy pocketfft)

fit_gate.pin_basis: sha256 over (float32 point, float64 loss, stage) of all 220 recorded evaluations

outcomes.metal: passes every gated metric at 128x128 and 512x512; best object relL2 5.618e-07
outcomes.mps: deterministic failures at 512x512 (object relL2 4.317e-06 against a 2.196e-06 bound; mps-vs-metal 4.179e-06) and at one recorded 128x128 setting (loss 2.875e-07 against a 2.24e-07 bound)
outcomes.mps_root_cause: fused math_mode and the MLX FFT realization are excluded by measurement; the excess is in the summed spectrum (per-BF weighting and complex64 accumulation). Line-level attribution unresolved.
outcomes.fit_trajectory: deterministic across processes (sha256 74cc777234a5ec107647ba0be60580c9abb58d0eca1ca3e6fd6b2cbeab93d72b); production optimize reproduces it exactly; the batched pair draw moves the optimum and is not the production path
outcomes.recorded_cached_vs_streamed_defect: closed in-tree by the ssb_ifft512_nyquist_correction; the cached half-plane path was the wrong one
